The old field names eeprom_status and checksum_status were two of the pointer bytes.

The dword is a word plus an i16 (all 6 accesses of 0x40af28 are lhz / sth; no lwz / stw; 8 decompiled uses ._0_2_). +0 is the speed governor fuel demand: lhz r29,0(r26) @ 0x2a650 and sth r28,0(r26) @ 0x2a900 (cm848_calculateProtectionLoadCompensation writes the PID result wStack_46), sth r31,-20696(r9) @ 0x2ab14 (initProtectionParamCalculation starts it at fuel_demand_computed), sth r11,-20696(r12) @ 0x2aba4 (cm848_processProtectionParamDelta clears it while governor_fuel_active_flag is 0), lhz r4,-20696(r4) @ 0x2bc74 (cm848_updateGovernorFromProtection compares it with engine_operating_mode_fuel_demand and copies it to operating_mode_governor_output.fuel_demand with mode_code 4). 0.0679 mm3 per stroke counts.

+2 i16 (7 decompiled uses ._2_2_; the old label row governor_integrator_state_b+2 has no type): sth r30,0(r27) @ 0x2a428 (cm848_calculateProtectionRpmFilter: (protection_monitored_rpm - engine_rpm_state.current_rpm, clamped to governor_integrator_lower_bound_cal / governor_integrator_upper_bound_cal) x governor_speed_gain_factor >> 14, filtered by cm848_signedFirstOrderFilter, clamped again; a clamp presets governor_integrator_working to the bound << 16), lha r30,-20694(r30) @ 0x2a524 and lha r9,-20694(r9) @ 0x2ab88 (signed loads: the PID load compensation multiplies it by the gain scale, and cm848_processProtectionParamDelta saves it as governor_integrator_prev_snapshot). The filtered, gain-scaled speed error, in 1/8 rpm units.

The word is two byte variables. +0 (0x3fed91) is a warm-up cycle counter modulo 40: engine_coolantTemp_overheat_monitor (stb r4,0(r5) @ 0x534238; lbz r11,0(r5) @ 0x53421c) adds 1 up to 0x27 then wraps to 0 once coolant_overheat_condition_flags is 3 (coolant above the sample taken at the end of the startup delay by more than 0x9ff / 64 = 40 deg F, and above 8960 / 64 = 140 deg F), then calls fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission; cm848_processFaultScanGroup (lbz r11,-4719(r11) @ 0x1d69c) stamps it into bits 10-15 of the fault status word (epoch << 10 | word & 0x3ff) and fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission (lbz @ 0x534064) clears every fault whose stamp equals it (status >> 10 == the count): a DTC erased after 40 warm-up cycles. The address is in the EEPROM mirror (0x3fd482-0x3feec1, EEPROM 0x190f) so it takes _cal under the brief rule.

+1 byte of the old word (0x3fed92; 16 byte accesses): fault_enqueueRecord (lbz r6,0(r4) @ 0x534cdc, stb r10,0(r4) @ 0x534ce8) uses it as the write index into fault_entry_ptr_queue (the 8-element queue at 0x3fed9c) and adds 1, tests == 8 for full; fault_updateActiveCounters (lbz r10,0(r30) @ 0x533cd8, stb r12,0(r30) @ 0x533dc0) subtracts 1 when it retires an entry; diag_resetSingleFault (stb r11,-4718(r12) @ 0x533ef4) clears it. Decompile prints it as (byte)fault_ring_epoch_counts / ._1_1_. EEPROM mirror address, so _cal.

text: Lead from fault_ring_epoch_counts: engine_coolantTemp_overheat_monitor (0x5341a8) is not a coolant overtemperature monitor. Its whole job is the OBD warm-up cycle count: coolant_overheat_condition_flags (0x40af07) bit 0 = coolant rose by more than 40 deg F (0x9ff counts of 1/64 deg F) above the sample DAT_003fd229, bit 1 = coolant above DAT_0005a9be (8960 = 140 deg F); at both bits it counts the cycle and runs fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission. Rename candidate cm848_countWarmUpCycleAndAutoClearFaults; flags bits warm_up_cycle_temperature_rise_reached_flag / warm_up_cycle_minimum_temperature_reached_flag. fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission is the erase after 40 warm-up cycles.

evidence: lha r11,-11735(r11) @ 0x5341d4 (engine_coolantTemp_overheat_monitor subtracts it from coolant_temp) and sth r11,-11735(r12) @ 0x534374 (cm848_mainLoopServiceMonitor stores sensor_readings.coolant_temp into it when fault_service_monitor_startup_delay_count reaches 0, decompile line 91140); 1/64 deg F. Copy window, no _cal (the ROM image holds 33536 as its initial value, never used).

lha r12,-22082(r12) @ 0x5341f0 (engine_coolantTemp_overheat_monitor: (int)DAT_0005a9be < (short)coolant_temp sets bit 1 of coolant_overheat_condition_flags); ROM word 8960 = 140 deg F (1/64 deg F counts); never written.

The dword is two words (all 6 accesses of 0x3fb5ae are sth / lhz; the next word 0x3fb5b0 is separate): +0 holds the injection_fuel_quantity_snapshot of the previous pass, not a crank period: hpcr_processEngineSyncPulses (lhz r9,0(r28) @ 0x453c4, sth r12,0(r28) @ 0x4542c) compares it with crank_sync_period_captured_threshold_cal before counting a crank period variation and then stores injection_fuel_quantity_snapshot into it (decompile lines 44775-44783); cm848_setEngineRunState3, cm848_engineRunState3Handler, cm848_engineRunState3HandlerWithTimebaseCapture (sth r9,-19026(r10) @ 0x44abc / 0x44df4 / 0x44f34) and mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators (sth r30,-19026(r11) @ 0x43e0c) clear it. 6 decompiled uses (._0_2_).

+2 word (6 decompiled uses ._2_2_; the old label row crank_tooth_event_count has no type): cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal (lhz r12,0(r30) @ 0x443b8, sth r3,0(r30) @ 0x443c8, sth r10,0(r30) @ 0x44404) adds 1 per pass while crank_period_countdown is 0 and engine rpm is non-zero, else clears it; at crank_sync_period_confirm_count_cal it sets fault_detected_bits_80_to_95 bit 0x1000 (fault 92) and clamps there, below it clears the bit; mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators clears it (sth r30,-19024(r11) @ 0x43dec). Same pattern as the neighbouring crank_sync_event_count (0x3fb5b2).

text: crank_sync_period_captured_threshold_cal (0x408f86, word) is a fuel quantity threshold, not a crank period one: hpcr_processEngineSyncPulses compares it with injection_fuel_quantity_snapshot_previous (the old crank_sync_period_captured) in the same test that checks crank_period_tooth_count_threshold_cal against crank_period_variation_metric. Rename lead: crank_period_variation_minimum_injection_fuel_quantity. crank_sync_period_confirm_count_cal (0x408f80) is the confirm count of crank_period_timeout_count.

evidence: The word is written one byte at a time (2 + 9 decompiled piece uses ._0_1_ / ._1_1_, 9 byte stores in the sweep) and read once as a whole halfword (lhz r11,-19512(r11) @ 0x39f14 in cm848_servicePciTransmit, copied to pci_controller_transmit_word 0x40b386). One whole-word write exists too (pci_controller_command_word = 0xaf8, decompile line 37126), so expect a cast there and at the copy to pci_controller_transmit_word (line 37129); leave that word as it is (it is assigned 0xe0 / 0xa18 / the command word as whole words). The row 0x3fb3c9 can_rx_message_type_code is a typeless boot-kernel label on the second byte; no boot-kernel code touches 0x3fb3c8 / 0x3fb3c9 in the sweep (all users are the PCI transmit path at 0x39c00-0x39f00).
